reviewType: independent AI exact-hash focused editorial-decision recheck
method: Checked each current decision, full source example and guide meaning, canonical brief and full-sentence live detector. For 3604 also tested whether regex match alone warrants aliasing despite different object/sense scope.

checks.sourceExample: She enjoys the buzz of physical shops on weekends.
checks.sourceGuideMeaning: The lively atmosphere of stores; a natural sensory collocation.
checks.canonicalTeachingMeaningEn: A feeling of excitement or pleasure, or an atmosphere of lively interest and activity.
checks.senseAndScopeEvidence: The physical shops are the setting; buzz itself is their lively atmosphere, precisely canonical 627.

checks.sourceExample: A repeated advertisement plants a seed in the mind.
checks.sourceGuideMeaning: Introduces an idea that may grow later; a fixed plant metaphor.
checks.canonicalTeachingMeaningEn: Introduce an idea or interest that may develop later.
checks.senseAndScopeEvidence: The advertisement introduces an idea that may develop, precisely canonical 022; in the mind is contextual wording.

checks.sourceExample: A new book can lift my mood.
checks.sourceGuideMeaning: Make me feel happier; a natural figurative phrase.
checks.canonicalTeachingMeaningEn: Make someone feel happier or more cheerful.
checks.senseAndScopeEvidence: A book improves mood, precisely canonical 181. The complete marked source phrase is matched.

checks.sourceExample: Teamwork lessons reach far beyond the court or the field.
checks.sourceGuideMeaning: Have effects outside sport; a distance metaphor.
checks.canonicalTeachingMeaningEn: To a much greater distance, extent or degree than a stated boundary or expectation.
checks.senseAndScopeEvidence: Lessons extend well outside the sports venue, precisely canonical 226 extent beyond a boundary.

checks.sourceExample: Only a handful of competitors reach the final.
checks.sourceGuideMeaning: Only a very small number; a fixed quantity idiom.
checks.canonicalTeachingMeaningEn: A small number of people or things, without specifying an exact count.
checks.senseAndScopeEvidence: Only modifies a handful of but does not change its small-number meaning, precisely canonical 323.

checks.sourceExample: The teacher will break them down into small steps.
checks.sourceGuideMeaning: Make complex ideas easier to understand by dividing them; a natural phrasal verb.
checks.canonicalTeachingMeaningEn: Divide a complex task into smaller, manageable parts.
checks.canonicalTargetPattern: \b(?:break|breaks|broke|broken|breaking) (?:it down|them down|the task down|the project down|down the task|down the project|down large tasks)\b
checks.senseAndScopeEvidence: The detector really does match break them down. Guide sense is simplifying complex ideas, while canonical 046 explicitly teaches dividing a complex task. Source pronoun lacks a clear antecedent in the isolated sentence, so a hold for sense/object scope remains justified.
checks.result: clear; corrected detector reason and hold justified

limits: AI peer review only; no human or release approval.
